description: Looking for teammates? Join HumanBeans and let’s create something awesome together. Into coding, web design, AI and any cool ideas you want to throw in. Bring your curiosity and energy, we’ll turn it into something great.
summary:
The first people to walk on Mars won’t have Google Maps, and out there a wrong turn could cost a lot more than time. We built Mars Survival Atlas to give them something close to it.

It’s an interactive map of Mars built on the real NASA/USGS Viking colour mosaic, with MOLA elevation shading. It marks all 9 places NASA has landed, plus science targets, polar ice and hazard zones. Every marker has a fact and a NASA source. You can pick any two places and get the distance and a safety score. If the direct path runs through a hazard, the map shows a detour. Navigation Mode splits a walk into legs with a compass bearing and walking time, so an astronaut can follow it step by step. An emergency button shows the quickest route back to a safe landing site.

We made it for astronauts planning a Marswalk, and for anyone curious about what surviving on Mars would really take. It runs in any browser.
details:
Mars Survival Atlas is an interactive map that helps astronauts explore Mars and plan safe journeys on its surface. It uses real NASA maps and elevation data to show 17 important locations, including landing sites, mountains, ice caps and dangerous areas.

The project includes several useful features, such as a Safe Route Finder, walking directions, safety scores, emergency return routes and a mission planner. It also has a Mars Guide in English and Roman Urdu to make learning about Mars easier for more people.

We built the project using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Leaflet.js. It runs directly in a web browser without needing installation or a server.

What makes our project special is that it is designed like a real survival tool, not just a map. It helps astronauts choose safer routes, estimate travel times and prepare for emergencies. We focused on astronaut safety, reliable NASA data, ease of use and accessibility. We also made sure to clearly label our own calculations and estimates.
